clauses.policy_sentence: Applicants must be an Australian citizen or have permanent residency status.
clauses.title: Residency

clauses.decides: Owns no residential property (a domestic or family violence exemption needs delegate approval).

missing.statement: The file has no property search outside the Northern Territory.

clauses.policy_sentence: Except in Remote Communities, Town Camps and CLAs, applicants and tenants who own or partly own residential property anywhere in Australia are ineligible for social housing.
clauses.title: Residential property ownership

clauses.decides: Whether income evidence is in the file. The Income and Assets policy is not bundled, so v1 does not test the thresholds.

missing.statement: The file holds no current income statement or employer remittance advice.

clauses.policy_sentence: If applying for urban social housing or private rental bond assistance, applicants must also qualify under additional income based criteria which are specified in the Income and Assets policy.
clauses.title: Income criteria for urban applicants

clauses.decides: A debt to the CEO (Housing) does not withhold housing.
clauses.policy_sentence: The provision of social housing will not be withheld based on a debt owed to the CEO (Housing).
clauses.title: Debts

clauses.decides: A tenancy terminated for breach in the last 2 years means ineligible for 2 years.
clauses.policy_sentence: Former social housing tenants who have had their tenancy agreement terminated or have voluntarily vacated the premises leaving sufficient evidence to justify a termination (under breach of tenancy agreement conditions or satisfactory tenancy criteria), are ineligible to apply for social housing for a period of 2 years, which includes property under the management or ownership of the CEO (Housing).
clauses.title: Unsatisfactory former tenancies

clauses.decides: The applicant falls in one of the four urgent-need categories.
policy_items: Young person in the care of the Chief Executive Officer Territory Families, Housing and Communities transitioning to independence;
Serious medical or social problems; and
clauses.policy_sentence: The following categories are considered an urgent need for social housing:
clauses.title: Urgent-need category

clauses.decides: Urgent need is proven with supporting documentation (see the Identification and Documentation policy).

missing.statement: The file holds no police record or protection order for the reported incident; the police attendance is known only from the support letter.

clauses.policy_sentence: Applicants must prove their urgent need for priority housing and are required to provide documentation that supports their claim for priority.
clauses.title: Urgent need documented

clauses.decides: Whether the "some discretion for extreme situations" applies.

missing.statement: Nothing in the file asks for, or records, use of the discretion for extreme situations.

clauses.policy_sentence: Priority housing applicants must meet the eligibility criteria for social housing, although the CEO (Housing) has some discretion for extreme situations.
clauses.title: Discretion for extreme situations

clauses.decides: Facts the writer found important that no clause names.
clauses.title: Not on the checklist

A-0142:p31:3.text: Declarant: Ms K. Subject: Housing history statement. After leaving the Palmerston tenancy, Ms K. rented privately. She returned the keys on the agreed closure date and later dealt with the account through Housing Accounts.

A-0142:p34:1.text: Ms K. and her children are staying with me in Darwin. I can accommodate them briefly, but I cannot provide a stable long-term room arrangement.

A-0142:p34:4.text: The host has offered a short stay in Darwin. The room is shared and crowded; there is no written tenancy or assured end date for the family.

A-0142:p34:5.text: The family may use the room while I can make it available, but the arrangement is informal and shared with my household. I cannot offer a separate bedroom or a fixed tenancy. Please ask through Ms K.'s agreed channel before contacting me about the stay, and do not circulate the location. I can confirm the start of the stay and the conditions described in this letter.

A-0142:p34:6.text: I will tell Ms K. promptly if the room availability changes. Until then, she and the children are managing with limited space for school things and ordinary daily routines. This note is my account of what I have offered; I have kept a copy with the date above. If a later confirmation is needed, I can provide it through the same protected channel.

A-0142:p35:1.text: My children and I have moved twice since the February incident. I keep their school clothing, medicines and essential papers in a small bag because our next safe place may change at short notice.

A-0142:p35:3.text: Declarant: Ms K. Subject: Applicant account of temporary moves. Since February, Ms K. and the children have moved twice. School clothing, medication and essential papers are kept ready because the next safe stay may change quickly.

A-0142:p36:1.text: I can host Ms K. and her children while they arrange another safe place. The room is shared and crowded, and I cannot offer a written tenancy or an assured end date.

A-0142:p36:4.text: The host can accommodate the family while another place is arranged, but cannot promise a separate room or a long-term stay. The host's location must remain confidential.

A-0142:p36:5.text: The family may use the room while I can make it available, but the arrangement is informal and shared with my household. I cannot offer a separate bedroom or a fixed tenancy. A-0142:p37:1.text: Our staff observed intermittent late arrivals after the children's sleeping arrangements changed. We offered both children a quiet place to settle at the start of the school day.

A-0142:p37:4.text: Staff offered Niko K. and Elia K. a quiet start to the school day. Arrival times have varied while the family has moved between temporary places.

A-0142:p37:6.text: Staff will continue the quiet arrival arrangement while the family moves between short stays. If the daily route becomes predictable, Ms K. can tell us whether the children need a different arrival plan. This note was prepared from school observations and the conversation with their parent. It is signed by the liaison and retained with the school contact record.

A-0142:p40:3.text: Subject: Ms K. Section: Household accommodation needs. Household or account name as shown on the application: Ms K. Locality for service: Darwin, Northern Territory. The requested home needs sleeping space for one adult and two children, access to transport and a location that avoids contact near the former home.

A-0142:p41:1.text: Ms K. permits her general practitioner to provide a short note about how instability affects her health. She does not consent to release of full clinical records.

A-0142:p42:1.text: We arranged an appointment for Ms K. to discuss disrupted sleep and anxiety following the move. With her consent, the practice will send a brief functional note.

A-0142:p42:4.text: The practice booked a consultation about disturbed sleep and anxiety following the move. Ms K. agreed to a brief housing-related functional note after the visit.

A-0142:p42:5.text: Ms K. has authorised a brief appointment confirmation and, after the consultation, a limited functional note. The practice will not send the full clinical file. A specific follow-up question can be put to the practice with fresh patient consent. Appointment details and clinical correspondence will each carry their own dates and signatures so they can be distinguished.

A-0142:p43:1.text: This limited clinical note records Ms K.'s reported sleep disruption and anxiety after the February incident, and the effect of repeated moves on her daily routine.

A-0142:p43:3.text: Patient: Ms K. Reason for letter: Clinical note cover. The GP note is confined to reported symptoms, daily functioning and the effect of unstable accommodation. Clinical history and treatment records remain with the practice.

A-0142:p43:4.text: The patient discussed daily functioning and the physical or emotional demands of the present accommodation during consultation. This limited note records matters relevant to sleeping, moving safely and maintaining a routine. It was prepared with the patient's consent for the housing office. No full clinical history, prescription chart or unrelated family information is enclosed.

A-0142:p44:1.text: Ms K. reports anxiety and disrupted sleep following the family violence incident; a stable and safe home would support treatment.

A-0142:p44:3.text: Patient: Ms K. Reason for letter: GP functional note. The patient reports waking often and finding it difficult to keep a regular routine while changing accommodation. Follow-up is planned at the next practice appointment.

A-0142:p44:4.text: The patient discussed daily functioning and the physical or emotional demands of the present accommodation during consultation. This limited note records matters relevant to sleeping, moving safely and maintaining a routine. It was prepared with the patient's consent for the housing office.
